title: I'm a programmer, but not a game dev. I run 5 Claude Code sessions like a tiny game studio. Here's one full run of our cat tower defense
author: qing-turn
selftext:
Hi from China! I'm a programmer, but I've never made a game before. I've loved games since I was a kid, and I've always wanted to make one that I'd love to play myself. For the last week I've been making this cat tower defense by running five Claude Code sessions, each with one job, like a tiny studio:

Designer: talks with me, turns my ideas into tasks, keeps one shared task list

Programmer: all the Unity / C# code, runs bot balance tests before every build

Artist: works with the human artists in our studio. They draw some of the base sketches, and AI (gpt-image-2) quickly turns them into usable sprites, then the frames get cut out and checked

Sound: makes most sound effects with code, music with MiniMax

Marketing: cut this video, and helped with the English in this post, because honestly my English isn't great. Sorry about that...

My job is to decide how the game should feel, play every build, and say "no, this feels wrong." And to throw every idea in my head at it. It feels like all the crazy ideas I've had can actually make it into the game, one by one, and I can test them really fast.

How it works: each session is its own agent. Most of the time I only talk to the Designer, and it hands out tasks to the Artist, Programmer and Sound sessions. It's been surprisingly smooth. By the end of day one I already had roughly the game you see in the video, and I've spent the rest of the week polishing it.

The game: put 10 of the same cat on the field and they merge into a Giant Cat, then you pick Form X or Form Y. 30 waves, and the last one has two Bosses at once. The video is one full run at normal speed, cut down to about 4 and a half minutes, with every Boss fight left uncut.

To be clear: AI is used heavily in the art, with human artists doing base sketches. It's not released yet and there's no store page.

Happy to answer questions about the setup, or anything else. Like... would you want to play it?!

comments.author: Old_Peak_1332
comments.body: cool! How did you get it set up like this? Do you use an IDE? What is the token usage?

replies.author: qing-turn
replies.body:
Thanks! No IDE really, it's all Claude Code in the terminal. Each session gets its own role description file (designer, programmer, artist, sound, marketing) and they can message each other, plus one shared task list that's the single source of truth. The programmer drives Unity from the command line, so nobody has to click around in the editor.

Token usage is honestly huge: roughly a billion tokens so far. Running 5 sessions in parallel all day adds up fast.
